Mechanisms summary of acquired resistance to chemotherapy

Mechanisms summary of acquired resistance to chemotherapy. Intrinsic mechanisms: DNA damage repair activation, ABC transporter-mediated drug efflux, lineage plasticity (Squamous differentiation, EMT, CSC enrichment), and metabolic/epigenetic reprogramming. Extrinsic mechanisms: Cytokine secretion by CAFs/TAMs that activates pro-survival pathways, and hypoxia-driven aberrant angiogenesis establishing a chemoprotective niche. ABC: ATP-binding cassette transporter; ACC: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase; BCRP: Breast cancer resistance protein; CAF: Cancer-associated fibroblast; CSC: Cancer stem cell; CTSH: Cathepsin H; EMT: Epithelial-mesenchymal transition; EpCAM: Epithelial cell adhesion molecule; FASN: Fatty acid synthase; FAT: Fatty acid translocase; HK: Hexokinase; HIF-1α: Hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha; IL-6: Interleukin-6; IL-10: Interleukin-10; KRT17: Keratin 17; LDHA: Lactate dehydrogenase A; MRP: Multidrug resistance-associated protein; NRP1: Neuropilin-1; OXPHOS: Oxidative phosphorylation; PFK: Phosphofructokinase; P-gp: P-glycoprotein; SOX2: SRY-Box transcription factor 2; STAT3: Signal transducer and activator of transcription 3; TAM: Ttumor-associated macrophages; TCA: Tricarboxylic acid; TGF-β: Transforming growth factor beta; TP63: Tumor protein p63; TWIST1: Twist Family bhlh transcription factor 1
